newsitem.title: USA: Employee Solutions dips on earnings fears.
newsitem.headline: Employee Solutions dips on earnings fears.

text.p: Shares of Employee Solutions Inc fell over 25 percent in heavy afternoon trading Thursday on fears the company may fall short of analysts' expectations when it reports fiscal fourth quarter earnings after the stock market closes.
Shares of the Phoenix, Ariz.-based company were off 5-1/4 at 14-5/8 on Nasdaq.
"There is a lot of nervousness about the company's earnings release," said Warren Albergotti, an analyst at The Volume Investor who follows the stock.
"There have been a lot of rumors that they are not going to be able to meet expectations," he said.
Analysts expect the company to earn $0.14 a share for the fourth quarter, begun last October 1, according to First Call.

"I am extremely confident they will meet analysts' expectations," Albergotti said. "I believe most of the rumors have been spread by short sellers who have plagued the stock for over two years. We've never been able to find a single shread of evidence to support any of them."
Stacey Kleven, an analyst at TIS Group, said the fall in the stock was due to the rumors, coupled with the heavy short position and a large holder selling the stock at market prices Thursday.

"It was a combination of the fact that they are getting ready to report earnings after the close today...the high short interest in the stock, and this company that had a significant stake dumping (their holdings)," Kleven said.
Officials at Employee Solutions, which provides worker leasing and worker compensation services, were not available for comment.
"The company is in better shape that it ever has been," Albergotti said.
